framing.overview: This module is the diagnostic layer behind the report: where enquiries reach Cedar Ridge, what happens to them on each route, and which of those routes is costing the most. It looks only at converting demand that already exists, because that is the part we can fix without changing what you spend on anything.

framing.expectedImpact: The realistic outcome is more of the enquiries you already receive turning into booked jobs, particularly the ones arriving in the evenings and at weekends where nothing currently catches them.

file1.executiveSummary: Cedar Ridge converts well once somebody is actually in the conversation, and the review record says so: competent work, honest advice, fair prices. Everything scoring badly in this report happens before that conversation starts. A call that rings out has no fallback, a form fill has nothing automated behind it, an evening enquiry has nowhere to land, and a quote that goes quiet depends on somebody remembering it. The largest recoverable figure sits on the phone line, and the cheapest fix sits on the same line.

growthAudit.overview: The audit covers the routes an enquiry can take into this business and what each one does when nobody is free. It does not cover how to get more enquiries, which is out of scope for this engagement by design.

findings.finding: One published line with no visible text-back path, and no record anywhere of how many calls are answered against how many are not.
The form collects four generic fields and has nothing automated behind it, so reply speed depends on the day's job list.
Google hours show evenings and weekends closed, with no booking path and no chat to catch demand in those hours.
No online scheduler on the site or the Google profile; every booking costs a phone conversation.
A social page is linked from the footer and sits outside every other channel, with no shared response standard.
4.5 stars across 58 reviews, with the work itself consistently well described.

technicalUx.businessImpactSummary: The page loads quickly enough that nothing in this report is being caused by it: 3.1 seconds to the main content on mobile and 1.5 on desktop. These numbers are context, not a work item, since site performance is not part of a conversion engagement.

revenueLeaks.issue: Calls that ring out have no automated recovery behind them.
revenueLeaks.whyItMatters: A caller who cannot reach a person typically dials the next company within minutes, and nothing brings them back.
revenueLeaks.recommendedFix: Missed-call text-back on the published line, replying within seconds.
revenueLeaks.expectedImpact: The largest single figure in this report, estimated beside that finding.

revenueLeaks.issue: An after-hours enquiry has nowhere to land.
revenueLeaks.whyItMatters: A burst line does not wait for office hours, which is exactly when the listing shows you closed.
revenueLeaks.recommendedFix: After-hours auto-response plus a booking page that stays open around the clock.
revenueLeaks.expectedImpact: Turns the highest-urgency hours into hours where you are the company that replied.

revenueLeaks.issue: Reply speed on the form is set by the day's schedule.
revenueLeaks.whyItMatters: A published review already describes an enquiry that waited, and it went elsewhere.
revenueLeaks.recommendedFix: Instant auto-reply and qualification behind every submission.
revenueLeaks.expectedImpact: First useful reply becomes yours on enquiries you are already receiving.

revenueLeaks.whyItMatters: a full re-pipe and a dripping tap get the same treatment, so the valuable one waits longest.
revenueLeaks.recommendedFix: Job type, urgency and service area captured and scored at the point of entry.
revenueLeaks.expectedImpact: The biggest job of the week is the first one somebody calls back.

revenueLeaks.issue: Quotes that go quiet depend on somebody remembering them.
revenueLeaks.whyItMatters: Decisions on planned work are made across weeks, and the company still present when the customer is ready usually gets the work.
revenueLeaks.recommendedFix: A multi-touch follow-up sequence on every unbooked quote, with a longer seasonal branch.
revenueLeaks.expectedImpact: Converts demand already earned, without adding a single new enquiry.

localMarketIntelligence.customerPsychology: Most people contacting a plumbing and drainage company are already uncomfortable and slightly anxious about the bill. They are not researching, they are triaging, and they read speed of reply as a proxy for competence.
localMarketIntelligence.buyingBehavior: Emergency work is decided in under an hour and usually by phone. A full re-pipe is decided over several weeks, often with two or three written quotes, and frequently stalls until something forces the issue.
localMarketIntelligence.trustExpectations: Licensing and insurance are assumed rather than persuasive. What actually moves a homeowner is another homeowner in their own neighbourhood saying the tradesperson was honest about what did not need doing.
localMarketIntelligence.competitiveSaturation: Nanaimo has a dense field of plumbing and drainage contractors, and the three nearest carry review counts between 87 and 141. Nobody in that set is visibly answering after hours.
localMarketIntelligence.seasonalDemand: Demand arrives in bursts around the first cold snap. Capture problems cost several times more inside those windows than they do in the quiet months.
localMarketIntelligence.priceSensitivity: Callout fees are compared closely; larger quotes are compared on trust and timing more than on the bottom line. A written price given quickly beats a slightly lower one that took three days.
localMarketIntelligence.credibilityMarkers: Years in the mid-Island, licensing, named plumbers, and reviews that mention specific streets or neighbourhoods rather than generic praise.

leadScoring.rubric: Job type, urgency, service area and property type, weighted so an urgent in-area job outranks everything else. Thresholds are reviewed monthly against jobs that actually booked.
leadScoring.hot: 90–100 · no hot water or a replacement-sized job inside the service area.
leadScoring.warm: 70–89 · a real job in the area with no immediate urgency.
leadScoring.cold: 0–69 · planning ahead, out of area, or work you do not take on.

executiveSummary.narrative: Missed calls with no recovery is the largest recoverable number in this report: an estimated CAD $487 a month, computed from the volumes and job value set out beside that finding and the industry rates cited with them. Underneath all of it sits one pattern: every route into Cedar Ridge ends at a person who has to be free at that exact moment, and nothing sits behind any of them when that person is on a job. What this business is missing is the layer between an enquiry arriving and somebody getting to it.
biggestOpportunities: Instant acknowledgement on the phone line and the form, which is the cheapest change on this list and touches every enquiry you already receive.
A bookable calendar that stays open through the evenings and weekends your listing currently shows as closed.
Scoring at the point of capture, so a full re-pipe stops waiting behind a dripping tap.
A past-customer list that has already bought from you once and is currently being contacted by nobody.
biggestThreats: A published review already describes an enquiry that got no reply, which is the one kind of review a homeowner reads as a warning.
Competitors in Nanaimo carry noticeably more review volume, which makes speed of reply the cheaper place for you to win.
Demand arrives in short bursts around the first cold snap, and capture problems cost the most in exactly those weeks.
mostUrgentFixes: Missed-call text-back on the main line.
Instant auto-reply and qualification behind the contact form.
After-hours auto-response covering evenings and weekends.
quickWins: Webchat that continues in SMS, so a small question does not need a phone call.
The social page inbox pulled into the same queue as calls and texts.
Call tracking switched on, so answered-versus-missed stops being a guess.

scorecard.overallReadout: Cedar Ridge converts well once a person is actually in the conversation. The reviews describe competent work at a fair price, and booked jobs get attended. Everything scoring low here sits in front of that conversation: the enquiry arriving, being acknowledged, being sorted and being followed up. That is a capture and response problem, not a reputation problem, and it is the cheaper of the two to fix.

leakAnalysis.evidence: There is no booking link on the site or on your Google Business Profile.
leakAnalysis.explanation: Every booking currently costs a phone conversation, which means it can only happen while somebody is free to have one. A homeowner who decides at 10pm to lock in a Saturday visit has to remember to call tomorrow, and remembering is where a lot of that intent quietly dies.
leakAnalysis.businessImpact: Booking capacity is capped by the hours somebody can spend on the phone rather than by the number of plumbers you can put on the road.
leakAnalysis.recommendedFix: We build the booking page inside your GoHighLevel sub-account, wire it to real plumber availability, and put it behind every call-to-action on the site so a visitor can take a slot without speaking to anyone.
allowedStats: 82% of consumers expect an 'immediate' response; 60% define immediate as 10 minutes or less (HubSpot State of Inbound).

leakAnalysis.evidence: The contact form collects a name, an email, a phone number and a free-text message. Nothing on it establishes what the job is, where it is, or how urgent it has become.
leakAnalysis.explanation: Every enquiry therefore arrives looking identical, so whoever reads the inbox has to phone each one back just to find out which is a full re-pipe and which is a dripping tap. That triage happens at whatever speed the day allows, and the big job waits in line behind the small one.
leakAnalysis.businessImpact: The most valuable enquiry in the inbox gets exactly the same treatment as the least valuable one, which means your biggest jobs routinely wait the longest.
leakAnalysis.recommendedFix: We rebuild the form around lead qualification so each enquiry is scored on job type, urgency and service area as it arrives, and a priority job pages the on-call plumber instead of joining a queue.

leakAnalysis.evidence: Your published number is a single line with no text-back path visible anywhere on the site. Most owner-run plumbing and drainage businesses let a call fall through to voicemail while the crew is on a job, which is the industry pattern being flagged rather than something we saw here.
leakAnalysis.explanation: A call that rings out is not a lost customer yet. It becomes one at the moment that homeowner dials the next company on their list, which is typically within a few minutes. Nothing on the site offers a text as a lighter alternative, so a caller who cannot get through has no second route back to Cedar Ridge.
leakAnalysis.businessImpact: Where this holds, every call that rings out is demand you have already paid for arriving and leaving without a record. Because nothing logs it, the size of the problem stays invisible until it is measured.

dollarImpact.leadVolumeBasis: Assuming 20 enquiries a month (our assumption, not a number we measured)
dollarImpact.avgValueBasis: CAD $174 replacement cost per lead — an industry benchmark (WordStream), converted from USD at a rate we hold fixed (our assumption, not a number we measured)
dollarImpact.formula: 20 enquiries (our assumption, not a number we measured) × 14% missed × CAD $174/lead = CAD $487/mo

leakAnalysis.recommendedFix: We put a missed-call text-back on the line so a caller who does not reach a person receives a message within seconds, and route their reply into the same qualification flow as a form fill.
allowedStats: Missed-call rates by industry: Healthcare 32%, Legal 28%, Home Services 14%, Real Estate 9% (CallRail).
85% of callers who reach voicemail never call back (CallRail Benchmark Report).
78% of customers have abandoned a business after an unanswered call; 82% say they'll call a competitor next (CallRail consumer survey).
Phone calls to home-services businesses convert ~10–15x more than web leads (BIA/Kelsey).
leakAnalysis.mathFrame: ≈ CAD $487/mo — assuming 20 enquiries a month (our assumption, not a number we measured) × a 14% home-services missed-call rate (CallRail) × CAD $174 replacement cost per lead, an industry benchmark (WordStream), converted from USD at a rate we hold fixed (our assumption, not a number we measured). Estimated; we run this with your real numbers at kickoff.

Phone calls to home-services businesses convert ~10–15x more than web leads (BIA/Kelsey).

leakAnalysis.area: No structured follow-up on unbooked leads
leakAnalysis.leakName: No structured follow-up on unbooked leads
leakAnalysis.evidence: What happens to a quote that goes quiet is not visible from outside, and we did not see it here. Most owner-run plumbing and drainage businesses stop after one or two attempts, which is the industry pattern being flagged rather than something we saw here.
leakAnalysis.explanation: A homeowner who asks for a price on a full re-pipe is often not ready to spend until the first cold snap forces the issue. If nothing reaches them between those two moments, the decision gets made without Cedar Ridge in the room. Where that pattern holds, the quote is not lost on price, it is lost on silence.
leakAnalysis.businessImpact: Quotes that went quiet are the cheapest pipeline you own, because the enquiry was already earned once. If that is how it works today, most of that pipeline is expiring untouched.
leakAnalysis.recommendedFix: We deploy a multi-touch follow-up sequence across email and SMS on every unbooked quote, spaced across the weeks the decision actually takes, with a longer branch for the ones who said not yet.
allowedStats: Most leads need several touches before they buy, and most businesses stop after one or two.
The average business takes ~42–47 hours to respond to a new lead (HBR/Drift).
leakAnalysis.mathFrame: Most leads need several touches before they buy, and most businesses stop after one or two.
leakAnalysis.industryPattern: Most leads need several touches before they buy, and most businesses stop after one or two. The average business takes ~42–47 hours to respond to a new lead (HBR/Drift).
leakAnalysis.kickoffLine: We verify this together at kickoff — if you already have this covered, it comes off the list.

leakAnalysis.evidence: 58 Google reviews point to years of completed jobs, so a list of past customers almost certainly exists somewhere. Most owner-run plumbing and drainage businesses never write to that list at all, which is the industry pattern being flagged rather than something we saw here.
leakAnalysis.explanation: A plumbing and drainage customer buys again on a schedule: a service visit most years, a replacement eventually. The households already on that list are the warmest demand in Nanaimo and the only demand you never have to compete for.
leakAnalysis.businessImpact: A dormant list is revenue that has already chosen you once. If nothing reaches it seasonally, that demand simply goes to whichever company reaches them first.
leakAnalysis.recommendedFix: We load the past-customer list into the pipeline and run a seasonal reactivation sequence ahead of the first cold snap, sent from your number so it reads as a reminder from their own plumber.
leakAnalysis.kickoffLine: We verify this together at kickoff — if you already have this covered, it comes off the list.

leakAnalysis.evidence: Whether enquiries are tracked in a pipeline is not something a scan can establish. Most owner-run plumbing and drainage businesses keep enquiries across an inbox, a notebook and somebody's memory, which is the industry pattern being flagged rather than something we saw here.
leakAnalysis.explanation: Without a shared record, an enquiry only really exists in the head of whoever took it. The callback promised on Tuesday then competes with Wednesday's emergency, and the one that loses is the one nobody can see.
leakAnalysis.businessImpact: You cannot manage a number you cannot see. Where enquiries are held informally, the loss shows up as a quiet flat month rather than as anything anybody can point at.
leakAnalysis.recommendedFix: We build the pipeline inside your GoHighLevel sub-account using the stages your business actually runs, so every enquiry has one home, one owner and one next action.
leakAnalysis.kickoffLine: We verify this together at kickoff — if you already have this covered, it comes off the list.

leakAnalysis.evidence: The site links out to a Facebook page. Most owner-run plumbing and drainage businesses answer those in an app on one person's phone, which is the industry pattern being flagged rather than something we saw here.
leakAnalysis.explanation: A message on a social page usually lands separately from the phone line and separately from the inbox. Where that is the case, it typically gets answered when that person next opens the app rather than when the customer sent it.
leakAnalysis.businessImpact: A channel nobody owns is a channel with no response time attached. Where enquiries arrive there, they are landing in a queue with no service level behind it.
leakAnalysis.recommendedFix: We connect the social page inbox into the same conversation view as calls, texts and form fills, so a direct message is answered on the same clock as everything else.
allowedStats: 82% of consumers expect an 'immediate' response; 60% define immediate as 10 minutes or less (HubSpot State of Inbound).
leakAnalysis.industryPattern: 82% of consumers expect an 'immediate' response; 60% define immediate as 10 minutes or less (HubSpot State of Inbound).
leakAnalysis.kickoffLine: We verify this together at kickoff — if you already have this covered, it comes off the list.

leakAnalysis.evidence: We did not scan for a payment or deposit mechanism, and none of this is visible from outside. Most owner-run plumbing and drainage businesses collect on site or by cheque, which is the industry pattern being flagged rather than something we saw here.
leakAnalysis.explanation: The distance between a customer saying yes and money actually moving is where jobs quietly slip. If a deposit depends on somebody standing in the house with a card reader, the job is not really committed until the morning it happens.
leakAnalysis.businessImpact: An uncommitted job is an easy job to postpone. Where nothing is paid up front, a cancellation costs the customer nothing and costs you the slot.
leakAnalysis.recommendedFix: We add a text-to-pay deposit link into the booking flow, so a slot is held by a real payment and next week's schedule stops being provisional.
leakAnalysis.kickoffLine: We verify this together at kickoff — if you already have this covered, it comes off the list.

leakAnalysis.evidence: Whether calls are tracked is not visible from outside. Most owner-run plumbing and drainage businesses keep no answered-versus-missed record at all, which is the industry pattern being flagged rather than something we saw here.
leakAnalysis.explanation: Without a record of how many calls came in and how many reached a person, the size of the capture problem is a matter of opinion. Every other fix in this report becomes easier to sequence the moment that number exists.
leakAnalysis.businessImpact: Where call volume is not recorded, staffing and capacity decisions get made without knowing how much demand never reached anybody.
leakAnalysis.recommendedFix: We turn on call tracking and recording across the numbers we deploy, so answered, missed and after-hours volume arrives as a number in the monthly report instead of a guess.

funnel.overview: This is the path an enquiry takes from the moment it arrives to the moment the plumber is standing at the door, and the version below is the one we build for you. Every stage that can run without a person waiting on it does. The two that cannot are the ones where judgement or a licensed trade is the whole point.

stages.role: Get every enquiry into one system regardless of which channel it arrived on.
stages.currentWeakness: Three separate routes into the business today, none of which share a queue: a phone line with no fallback, a form with nothing behind it, and a social page sitting on its own.
stages.whatWeDeploy: One tracked number with missed-call text-back, a webchat widget that continues in SMS, the social inbox connected, and the site form rewritten to feed the same queue.
stages.kpi: Share of inbound enquiries that reach the system with a timestamp on them.

stages.role: Score and sort every enquiry before a human spends a minute on it. This is the stage we run for you every month.
stages.currentWeakness: The form collects a name, an email, a phone number and a message, so every enquiry looks identical and triage happens by phone.
stages.whatWeDeploy: Scoring on job type, urgency and service area at the point of capture, with routing rules that page the on-call plumber for priority work and hold the rest for the office.
stages.kpi: Median time from enquiry to a scored, routed lead.

stages.role: Make sure the first reply is ours, on every channel, every time.
stages.currentWeakness: A review describes an enquiry through the site that waited days, and nothing automated sits behind that form today.
stages.whatWeDeploy: Instant auto-reply on form and chat, missed-call text-back on the phone, and an after-hours response that covers the evenings and weekends your listing shows as closed.
stages.kpi: Median first-response time, measured in minutes rather than hours.

stages.role: Stay present between the quote and the decision, and between one job and the next.
stages.currentWeakness: What reaches an unbooked quote is not visible from outside, and most local trades stop after one or two attempts.
stages.whatWeDeploy: A multi-touch email and SMS sequence on every unbooked quote, a longer branch for the not-yet leads, and a seasonal reactivation run at the past-customer list.
stages.kpi: Share of quoted jobs that book within ninety days.

stages.role: Let a ready customer hold a real slot without needing a phone conversation.
stages.currentWeakness: Booking runs through phone and email only, so it can only happen while somebody in the office is free.
stages.whatWeDeploy: The booking page inside your GoHighLevel sub-account, wired to plumber availability, with a text-to-pay deposit link that turns a held slot into a committed one.
stages.kpi: Share of bookings taken without a phone call.

stages.role: Protect the booked slot and pick up the ones that fall over.
stages.currentWeakness: Nothing between the booking and the visit currently reminds anybody, and the wait grows as booking moves online.
stages.whatWeDeploy: Confirmation and reminder messages on every booking, a same-day text before arrival, and a two-step recovery sequence on any appointment that does not happen.

crmPipeline.overview: One pipeline, six stages, and a rule for what moves an enquiry between them. The point is that at any moment you can see how many jobs are sitting at each stage and who owes the next action, which is the thing an inbox can never tell you.

stages.entryCriteria: Any first contact at all — a form, a call, a chat on the site, a message on Facebook or Instagram, a text to your number.
stages.exitCriteria: Somebody works out what they want and moves them on, or the follow-up sequence runs its course without them booking.
stages.ownership: Automation, with the office notified on priority scores.
stages.reviewProcess: Anything sitting here more than fifteen minutes during business hours raises an alert.

stages.entryCriteria: The qualifying questions come back with an answer worth your time, or you talk to them and decide it is worth pursuing.
stages.exitCriteria: They take a time on the calendar, or they go quiet and drop into follow-up.
stages.ownership: Office, working from the score and the answers behind it.
stages.reviewProcess: Reviewed daily; anything over two days without a quote gets chased.

stages.entryCriteria: An appointment is confirmed — booked by them online, or put in by you or your team.
stages.exitCriteria: The appointment happens, or it does not.
stages.ownership: Automation for the reminders, dispatch for the scheduling.
stages.reviewProcess: Checked each morning against the day's route.

stages.entryCriteria: The appointment is marked as attended.
stages.exitCriteria: They go ahead, or they decide against it.
stages.ownership: The plumber on site, with the office picking up the paperwork.
stages.reviewProcess: Reviewed at the end of each day against what was on the calendar that morning.

stages.entryCriteria: They say yes — or a deposit lands, which says yes for them.
stages.exitCriteria: It does not. This is the end of the line, and reaching it is what asks the customer for a review.
stages.reviewProcess: Review request fires automatically once the job is marked complete.

stages.entryCriteria: They say no, they go elsewhere, or the 60-day follow-up sequence finishes without a booking and closes them out.
stages.exitCriteria: They come back in as a New Lead the day they get in touch again — nothing is deleted, the history stays with them.
stages.reviewProcess: Nothing is deleted — the record stays with its history and the seasonal reactivation run picks it up again.

faq.question: How quickly can somebody get here?
faq.answer: Urgent no hot water calls are usually same day. Everything else is normally within the same week, and you will be given a real window rather than a vague morning or afternoon.

faq.question: What does it cost to have somebody look at it?
faq.answer: There is a callout fee for the visit, quoted to you before it is booked, and it comes off the bill if you go ahead with the work. Nothing starts without a written price you have agreed to.

faq.question: What happens if I message you in the evening?
faq.answer: You get an acknowledgement within a minute confirming we have it, and a real reply first thing. If it is an emergency, the message routes to the on-call plumber rather than waiting for the office to open.

faq.question: Which areas do you cover?
faq.answer: Nanaimo and the mid-Island. If you are outside that we will say so straight away rather than leaving you waiting on a callback.

faq.question: Should I repair the hot water tank or replace it?
faq.answer: That depends on age, what has failed and what the repair costs against a replacement. The plumber will give you both numbers and tell you honestly which one they would choose.

leadCaptureForm.emergencyRoute: If it is an emergency, call 250-555-0143 — it will route straight to the on-call plumber instead of waiting on a sequence.

leadGate.where: GoHighLevel → Sites → Forms → qualifying questions, and the on-screen replies LeadGate gives
leadGate.openingLine: Five quick questions so the right person calls you back with the right answer, instead of phoning to work out what the job is.
questionIntros: This one decides whether it goes to the on-call plumber tonight or to the office in the morning.
Knowing the make and rough age of the hot water tank means the plumber arrives carrying the likely part.
The postal area tells us straight away whether you are inside the service area — if you are not, we will say so rather than leave you waiting.
leadGate.priorityAcknowledgement: That sounds like it cannot wait. The on-call plumber has been paged and will call you on this number — if it is a full outage, ring 250-555-0143 as well rather than waiting.
leadGate.standardAcknowledgement: Thanks — that is everything we need. Somebody from the office will call you back within the hour during business hours, or first thing tomorrow if you sent this overnight.

webchat.where: GoHighLevel → Sites → Chat widget (the bubble on your website)
webchat.greeting: Hi — this is Cedar Ridge. Ask away and somebody will answer. If you have no hot water, say so and it goes to the on-call plumber.
webchat.detailsAsk: Can I take a name and a mobile number? That way we can carry on by text if you have to close the tab, and nothing gets lost.
webchat.awayMessage: The office is closed but this is monitored. Send it through and you will get a real reply first thing. If it is urgent, call 250-555-0143 and it routes straight to the on-call plumber. You can also grab a slot now: [booking link]

siteAdvisory.where: Hand this to whoever looks after your website — it is advice, not work we do
siteAdvisory.scopeNote: These are advisory notes for whoever maintains the website; the page we build and host is the GoHighLevel booking page.
standingRules: These are advisory notes for whoever maintains the website; the page we build and host is the GoHighLevel booking page.
The fastest version of all of this is repointing the existing buttons at the booking page and leaving the rest of the site alone.
Never publish a review, a name or a photo that did not come from a real customer, however good the placeholder reads.
Any response time promised on the page has to match what the automation actually does, or the page becomes a liability.
siteAdvisory.summary: The page does the honest things well: the headline says what you do and where, and the phone number is a real tap-to-call link in the HTML rather than typed-out digits. What it does not do is give a visitor any way to act outside the hours your office is open. Measured on mobile the page scores 71 with a largest contentful paint of 3.1 seconds, and 90 at 1.5 seconds on desktop — real numbers, worth knowing, and context rather than a recommendation. The conversion read is that the page is quick enough that nothing on this list is being caused by load time.

notes.whatWeSaw: The two routes into the business we can find in the page HTML are a request-a-quote link to the contact form and a tap-to-call link to the main line. Both of those routes need the office to be open.
notes.recommendation: Point the existing buttons at the booking page and keep one visible at every scroll position. This is the cheapest change on the list and the one with the most behind it.

notes.whatWeSaw: The headline describes the trade and the service area accurately, with the licensing line directly beneath it. It does not answer the question a visitor arrives with, which is how quickly somebody can be there.
notes.recommendation: Lead with response and availability, and move the licensing line down to the proof row where it still does its job.

notes.whatWeSaw: The proof section states the rating and the review count in a sentence. There is no review text on the page and no named customer anywhere.
notes.recommendation: Pull three real Google reviews onto the page verbatim, each with a first name and a neighbourhood, and place one immediately under the hero.

notes.whatWeSaw: The form asks four generic questions — name, email, phone and a message box — so every submission looks identical until somebody phones back to find out what it is.
notes.recommendation: Add job type, urgency and postal area to the form. It is what lets an enquiry be sorted before anybody picks up a phone.

notes.whatWeSaw: Nothing beside either button tells a visitor when to expect an answer, and your listing shows evenings and weekends closed.
notes.recommendation: State the response commitment next to the button — and only a commitment the automation behind it actually keeps.

notes.whatWeSaw: Form submissions and tap-to-call clicks are not recorded as separate events, so there is no way to tell which route people actually take.
notes.recommendation: Track the two as separate conversion events and tag every enquiry with the hour it arrived. That is the only way to size the after-hours question with real data rather than a benchmark.

assets.trigger: A form is submitted — on your website, on your booking page, or anywhere else the form is placed.
assets.where: GoHighLevel → Automation → Workflows → Instant Lead Response

messages.timing: Within about a minute of the form arriving, day or night
messages.body: Hi [First name], it is Cedar Ridge. We have your message about [Job type] and somebody will call you back. If it cannot wait, reply URGENT and it goes to the on-call plumber.

messages.timing: Sent in the same minute as the text above
messages.subject: We have your message — Cedar Ridge
messages.body:
Hi [First name],

Thanks for getting in touch. We have your message about [Job type] and it is in the queue with a real person's name against it.

During office hours somebody will call you back within the hour. Outside them you will hear from us first thing.

If you would rather just hold a slot, you can pick one here: [booking link]

— The team at Cedar Ridge

assets.trigger: A call to your business number rings out unanswered, or lands in voicemail.
assets.where: GoHighLevel → Automation → Workflows → Missed Call Text-Back

messages.step: Step 1 · text, within seconds of the missed call
messages.timing: Fires the moment a call is not answered
messages.body: Sorry we missed you — this is Cedar Ridge. Tell us what is happening and we will call you straight back. If it is urgent, reply URGENT and it pages the on-call plumber.

assets.trigger: A call or a message arrives outside your opening hours — an evening, a weekend, a holiday.

messages.timing: Any enquiry between 4:30pm and 8am, or at a weekend
messages.body: Thanks — this is Cedar Ridge. The office is shut but this is monitored. You will get a real reply first thing. If it cannot wait until then, reply URGENT.

messages.timing: Sent alongside the text above
messages.subject: We have it — Cedar Ridge
messages.body:
Hi [First name],

Your message came in outside office hours and we have it. Somebody will be back to you first thing.

If you would rather hold a slot now, the calendar is open: [booking link]

— The team at Cedar Ridge

assets.trigger: An appointment is cancelled or rescheduled, by the customer or by you.
assets.where: GoHighLevel → Automation → Workflows → Appointment Cancelled — Stop Reminders

messages.timing: The moment an appointment is cancelled
messages.body: That is cancelled and no more reminders will come through. Whenever it suits, you can pick a new slot here: [booking link] — Cedar Ridge

assets.trigger: A new enquiry scores as high intent — the job type, the urgency or the size crosses the line you set with us.
assets.where: GoHighLevel → Automation → Workflows → Owner Hot-Lead Notification — this one goes to the owner's phone, never to the customer

messages.step: Step 1 · internal text to the owner
messages.timing: Within seconds of a priority-scored enquiry arriving
messages.body: Priority lead: [First name], [Job type], [Postal area]. Scored [Score]. Nobody has called them yet. Full record in the pipeline.

assets.trigger: Somebody sends a message to your Facebook page or your Instagram account.
assets.where: GoHighLevel → Automation → Workflows → Social DM Capture — the first reply, sent inside Facebook or Instagram

messages.step: Step 1 · reply in the social inbox
messages.timing: Within a minute of the message arriving
messages.body: Hi [First name] — this is Cedar Ridge. Happy to help. Can I take a mobile number so we can carry this on by text and get somebody out to you? If it is urgent, say so and it goes to the on-call plumber.

assets.trigger: A lead is marked as agreed, or a booking needs a deposit before the slot is held.

messages.step: Step 1 · text with the deposit link
messages.timing: Once the slot is agreed and the job is written up
messages.body: Hi [First name], that is [Date] between [Window]. The deposit link is here: [payment link]. Once it is paid the slot is held and you will get the confirmation. — Cedar Ridge

assets.trigger: You hand the list over once and we send it in batches, then it runs again on whatever rhythm you agree — usually seasonal.

messages.timing: Sent ahead of the first cold snap
messages.subject: Worth a look before the first cold snap
messages.body:
Hi [First name],

It has been a while since we were out. Ahead of the first cold snap it is worth a look at the hot water tank before it becomes an emergency call.

If you want one booked in, the calendar is here: [booking link]

— The team at Cedar Ridge

messages.timing: Four days after the email, only to those who did not book
messages.body: Hi [First name], it is Cedar Ridge. Still worth getting the hot water tank looked at before the first cold snap? Slots are here: [booking link]

messages.timing: Ten days after step 1, and the last message in the run
messages.subject: Last one from us this season
messages.body:
Hi [First name],

Last message from us on this. If you would rather we checked back next year instead, reply LATER and we will leave you be until then.

— The team at Cedar Ridge

assets.trigger: A new Google review is posted about your business.
assets.where: GoHighLevel → Reputation → Reviews → the reply posted publicly under each new review

messages.timing: Drafted the same day the review lands, sent once you approve it
messages.body: Thanks [First name] — glad we got that sorted for you. If anything else comes up, you know where we are. — Cedar Ridge

messages.timing: Drafted the same day, sent once you approve it
messages.body: Thanks for taking the time, [First name]. Sounds like the work was fine but getting hold of us was not. That is the part we are fixing. — Cedar Ridge

messages.timing: Drafted the same day, sent once you approve it
messages.body: [First name], that is not the standard we hold ourselves to and we would like to put it right. Call the office on 250-555-0143 and ask for whoever is on today. — Cedar Ridge
